subject.title: fix(plugins): plugins.deny is bypassed by a mixed-case manifest id

question: Should OpenClaw reject mixed-case external manifest IDs as invalid, or silently canonicalize them and own a migration across runtime exports and persisted plugin lifecycle records?
rationale: Both choices close the security bypass, but they define different external plugin and upgrade contracts; current documentation and tests do not establish permission to silently remap an existing plugin identity.

options.title: Reject Mixed-Case IDs
options.body: Fail manifest validation with an actionable lowercase-ID diagnostic and add upgrade or doctor guidance for already installed non-canonical plugins.

options.title: Migrate Every Identity Surface
options.body: Retain silent canonicalization only after normalizing runtime and persisted lifecycle ownership consistently and proving fresh-install plus upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Reject Mixed-Case IDs
recommendation.body: Fail manifest validation with an actionable lowercase-ID diagnostic and add upgrade or doctor guidance for already installed non-canonical plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available recent history spans the manifest and persisted installation boundaries involved in this contract decision.
